key_findings: RESOLVED: 'PlayAnimationOnActor' (0x00DA) is a misnomer. The opcode does NOT directly trigger an animation. The handler builds a battle-effect action record, selects a visual class via BattleResultEffectVisualClassSelector, packages it as a log entry, and posts it to a subscriber/queue dispatcher. The actual animation playback happens DOWNSTREAM in a separate poll loop (likely the actor tick or animation system reads from the queue).

ARCHITECTURAL: 0x00DA + 0x00E0 + 0x00E1 ALL route through the same FUN_0058C690 BattleEffectActionRecord builder. They differ in caller wrappers (0xDA via FUN_0058CAD0 with defaults; 0xE0 via FUN_0058CAF0; 0xE1 via FUN_0058CB40 - the 4 callers of FUN_0058C690 are FUN_0058CAD0/CAF0/CB40/CCA0). All three opcodes are battle-effect-visual triggers, not generic animation requests.

CROSS-PIPELINE LINK: The LogEntryBuilder + LogEntryDispatcher (BCS-Y-1009/1010) functions previously cataloged (as the CharaElement slot 8 sub-op 0x64 handlers) are SHARED with the slot 9 third-router action-record path. Suggests a unified actor event log structure consumed by multiple downstream subsystems.
